summary: Ludo Rocher was an Indologist who studied at Ghent University (~1944–1952). He held posts at Deccan College (1953–1955), the Free University of Brussels (~1953–1966), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1966–2016).

Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist who studied at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring (~1924–1928) and Humboldt University of Berlin under Heinrich Lüders (~1932–1935). In 1950, he assumed a chair at the University of Hamburg.
Ludwig Heller was an Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1888–1894). He held a post at the University of Greifswald from around 1902 to 1933.

Ludwig Lange worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig University and the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey (~1843–1847), later holding posts at Göttingen (~1847–1853), Charles University (~1853–1859), Giessen (~1859–1871), and Leipzig (~1871–1885).

Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at TU Berlin, the University of Manchester, and the University of Cambridge's Trinity College (~1911–1913). He held posts at Trinity College (1929–1947) and the University of Cambridge (1939–1947).
Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer. He held a post as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.

Luigi Suali was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Bologna (~1900–1904) and under Hermann Jacobi (~1905–1908). He held a post at the University of Pavia from around 1911 to 1951.

Luis Oscar Gómez was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Puerto Rico, Yale under Stanley Insler (~1963–1967), and Michigan. He held posts at Michigan (~1973–2008) and the Mangalam Research Center (~2008–2017).

Luise Hercus was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St Anne's College (~1944–1948) and the Australian National University. She served as a Reader in the Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies at ANU from around 1969 to 1991.
Lungten Dubgyur works in Tibetology and other fields. He completed degrees at Sherubtse College, Government Law College in Mumbai, and the University of Edinburgh.
Lungtok Tenpai Nyima was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He founded Menri Monastery and served as its abbot and throne-holder from around 1969 to 2017.

Lynn A. Struve is a sinologist and historian. She studied at the University of Washington (~1963–1967) and the University of Michigan (~1970–1976), and held a post at Indiana University from around 1977 to 2010.

Lynn Thomas is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Lancaster University and completed a D.Phil at the University of Oxford in 1987. She was attested as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton in 1997.

Léon Feer was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at INALCO under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux. He held posts at INALCO (1865), the Collège de France (1869–1872), and the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1872).

Léon Vandermeersch was a sinologist and philosopher who studied at INALCO, Paris Law Faculty, Faculty of Arts of Paris, EPHE, and Paris Diderot. He held posts at Aix-Marseille I (~1966–1973), Paris Diderot (~1973–1979), and EPHE (~1979–1993).
M. D. Balasubrahmanyam was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University, completing a dissertation in 1969. He also held an attested post there in 1967.

M. H. Krishna was an Indologist and historian who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1907–1911). He served as Professor of History at the University of Mysore, where his post is attested in 1910.
M. M. McCabe is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge from around 1966 to 1975. She held a post at King's College London from around 1990 to 2014.

M. N. Srinivas was an Indologist who studied at Mumbai under G. S. Ghurye and at Oxford. He held posts at Baroda College (~1951–1959), Delhi University (~1959–1972), and founded the Institute for Social and Economic Change, serving as chairman (attested 1998).
M. R. Raghava Varier is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Calicut and later held a post there as Reader in Epigraphy.
